metadata.title: The Hills Mechanism and the Galactic Center S-stars

evidence.quote: The flight time of the Koposov star suggests that this process must be efective within 10 Myr.
Koposov et al. (2020) hypervelocity star from the Galactic center (4.8 Myr).
In particular, Koposov et al. (2020) discovered a hypervelocity star that was ejected from the Galactic center 5 Myr ago, with a velocity vector consistent with the disk.
This star is noteworthy because, of all of the known hypervelocity stars, it has the strongest case for a Galactic center origin (see Figure 5 of Koposov et al. 2020).
For comparison, we also show the velocity of the hypervelocity star detected by Koposov et al. (2020).

notes: Koposov star (T:p1-b6; T:p10-b4; T:p19-b5): the paper supplies no catalog designation and refers to the previously identified Koposov et al. (2020) hypervelocity star. It is included as follow-up; no other individually identified star is treated as a Galactic unbound candidate.

Koposov star: The paper discusses the Koposov star (Koposov et al. 2020) as a hypervelocity star with a flight time of 4.8 Myr and a velocity vector consistent with the clockwise disk (T:p1-b11, T:p10-b4). Its ejection velocity is shown in Figure 16 as a purple star near 1700 km/s, and it is stated to be in the 92nd percentile of the ejection velocity distribution (T:p19-b5). However, the paper does not report values for any of the target quantities (ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper_motion_ra, proper_motion_dec, radial_velocity, galactocentric_radius, galactic_rest_frame_velocity, bound_probability, unbound_probability) for this star.
